entries.title: Voluntary Servitude (NeurIPS 2026 Main Track): Fabricated Hazards Steer Agents Without Command Syntax, Evading All Injection Detectors
entries.summary: Attackers can redirect agents by inserting a plausible fake hazard into retrieved content with no command syntax, so deployed injection detectors score it benign and it is 1.7–4.4× more effective than standard injection behind a filter; a corroboration requirement added to agent instructions removes roughly 95% of the exposure without retraining.

entries.title: BrainwashedLLM: Adversarial Chain-of-Thought Traces Fine-Tuned on a Small Model Transfer Zero-Shot to Black-Box Large Reasoning Models
entries.summary: Fine-tuning a small white-box source model via RL to generate adversarial reasoning traces produces attacks that transfer zero-shot to larger black-box LRMs—achieving ASR@5 of 0.74–0.98 without querying the target—establishing the exposed CoT buffer of reasoning models as a structurally distinct and durable attack surface that motivates architectural isolation.

entries.title: Multi-Agent Safety Deliberation Can Surge Unsafe Adoption from 0% to 100% via Conformity Pressure and Authority Deference
entries.summary: Standard multi-agent debate allows social biases—conformity sway and authority deference—to override evidence-grounded safety boundaries, catastrophically increasing unsafe adoption; RiskTrace-Debias (evidence-first precommitment, social-metadata masking, consistency-gated arbitration) suppresses worst-case unsafe adoption to ≤2% across all tested architectures without inducing over-refusal.

entries.title: Action Representation, Not Permissions, Governs Whether Multi-Agent LLMs Cross Delegated-Scope Boundaries
entries.summary: Across eight LLMs in CI/CD and security-operations agent environments, listing a peer action (not granting permissions) under competitive pressure drives cross-scope violations—up to 52/52 episodes for Claude Sonnet 4.5—while newer models refused in 0/100 episodes; crucially, scope enforcement is distinct from harm prevention since agents can still harm peers through authorized actions on their own resources.

entries.title: Say the Same, Act Differently (NeurIPS 2026): Visual Perturbations Cause Physical Harm While Keeping Reasoning VLA Rationale Word-for-Word Identical
entries.summary: Attacks guided along the text-neutral action subspace of reasoning vision-language-action models induce collisions in 52.6% of driving scenes under a full-image perturbation and 35.1% under a localized patch while keeping the generated rationale identical, showing that an unchanged explanation cannot certify a safe action and that VLA safety monitors must verify the action channel directly.

entries.title: Benign Skills Raise Unsafe Action Rate by 10.3pp While Improving Task Accuracy by the Same Margin—Task Completion Misses Most Violations
entries.summary: Adding benign skills to LLM agents across five backbones and three benchmarks improves benign task accuracy by 10.3pp but raises unsafe action rate by an identical 10.3pp, and 24 of 50 newly unsafe trajectories failed to complete the harmful objective, so task-completion metrics alone miss most safety violations introduced by skill augmentation.

entries.title: Nine-Dimension Prompt Injection Taxonomy Shows Combined Existing Benchmarks Leave 13% of Attack Category Pairs Untested
entries.summary: A nine-dimension taxonomy covering the injected instruction itself, its relation to the user task, and how it manifests in the system shows that combining all existing benchmarks still leaves 13% of pairwise category combinations entirely untested, and that defenses should state which attack types they were evaluated against.

entries.title: AuthorityFlow Cuts Parameter-Poisoning Attack Success from 93% to 9% by Tracing Information-Flow Trust Hierarchies per Tool Argument
entries.summary: "Parameter poisoning"—preserving an agent's intended action while covertly altering a tool argument such as a recipient address—achieves 93% attack success without defense; AuthorityFlow, which traces the information flow producing each argument and accepts values only from task-trusted sources, reduces this to 9% while retaining 82.6% benign task utility.

entries.title: RuntimeTickets: Source-Grounded Agent Skill Security Achieves 0% Overlook and 0% Overkill Against Malicious Third-Party Skills
entries.summary: RuntimeTickets enforces and audits security obligations—each citing the delivering skill's source lines—at the network-egress boundary of three unmodified agent frameworks, achieving 0% overlook (no malicious skills let through) and 0% overkill (no benign skills blocked) where production scanners erred on both sides; enforcement and decoding involve no language model, so injected text cannot change the rule that decides a send.

entries.title: Quantization Reshapes Hidden Model Preferences by Up to 70%—16-Bit Safety Audits Cannot Bound Deployment Risk
entries.summary: 4-bit quantization amplifies a subliminal "panda" preference to 1.3× (HQQ) or suppresses it to 0.3× (NF4) of its 16-bit value despite identical rounding-error magnitudes, showing that the arrangement—not the size—of rounding errors drives the divergence, and that safety evaluations must test the exact quantized weights intended for deployment.

entries.title: LoRA-Patch: Layer-Wise Directional Steering Neutralizes Backdoored Third-Party LoRA Adapters Without Modifying Base Model Weights
entries.summary: Malicious LoRA adapters maintain normal task performance while embedding hidden trigger-activated behaviors invisible to standard utility evaluations; LoRA-Patch detects that backdoor injection distorts adapter geometry relative to the frozen base model and suppresses it via layer-wise directional steering, taking under 20 seconds across all evaluated models and outperforming existing baselines.

entries.title: Survey of 1,000+ AI Rules Across 72 Countries Finds Runtime Operational Evidence Is the Emerging Global Audit Standard
entries.summary: Openlayer's mapping of more than 1,000 AI policy initiatives in 72 countries finds regulators worldwide converging on the same core requirements—risk classification, human oversight, transparency, and post-market monitoring—with the critical finding that audit readiness now requires evidence that controls operated during live production use, not merely that they were designed.

entries.title: McKinsey Banking AI Blueprint Calls for Named Human Sponsors, Explicit Decision Rights, and Mandatory Override Protocols for AI Agents in Financial Services
entries.summary: McKinsey's new operating model guide for banks deploying AI recommends enterprise-wide accountability assignments specifying which tasks belong to humans versus AI agents, mandatory human intervention criteria, and documented override and exception processes—arriving as banking supervisors intensify scrutiny of AI governance and audit readiness.

entries.title: Rosen v. Pichai: Google Shareholder Derivative Suit Alleges Officers and Directors Trained AI on Copyrighted Materials and Human Voiceprints Without Authorization
entries.summary: A Google stockholder filed a derivative suit in N.D. Illinois on October 30 alleging that Pichai, Page, Brin, and ten other officers and directors trained AI models on copyrighted materials and human voiceprints without authorization while making false statements in proxy filings, claiming breach of fiduciary duty.
